page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-16 is a compute instance configured within the flexible Standard shape family. The instance provides 8 virtual central processing units derived from 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor with dedicated core allocation. Operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, each core executes two threads. The system includes 16.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 2.0 GB per virtual CPU.

The hardware configuration features a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, categorizing it for compute-focused requirements. Local storage is not attached to this shape, meaning persistent disks or block storage volumes must be provisioned independently over network interfaces. There are zero GPU accelerators included in this configuration. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external host reachability.

This server structure provides high processing density relative to memory capacity. Because execution relies entirely on remote block storage, I/O-intensive database caching is constrained by network storage configuration and the moderate 16.0 GB memory footprint. VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-16 is targeted toward CPU-intensive tasks such as continuous integration workers, batch computing, API proxies, and standard web application hosting.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-16 is an x86_64 compute instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at 3.9 GHz with simultaneous multithreading, it delivers a focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance features no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data requirements. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned by default. Given the elevated CPU clock frequency and moderate memory allocation, the configuration favors processing workloads over large in-memory footprints. VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-16 is suited for batch processing, web serving, microservices, and general compute-bound enterprise applications.
